name: argyll-cms
why: Colour management suite that profiles real monitors with a sensor, a hands-on look at how colour is measured.

brief.what_it_is: Argyll CMS is an open source, ICC compatible color management system, distributed as a collection of C source code that compiles into a set of command line tools. It creates ICC profiles for scanners, cameras and film recorders, and calibrates and profiles displays and RGB and CMYK printers, using its own drivers for color measurement instruments. It also builds device links, including 3D LUTs and video calibration standards, and accepts spectral sample data with a choice of illuminants and observer types. Gamut mapping and profile linking use the CIECAM02 appearance model.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Graeme Gill, frames it as making serious color management available on platforms other than MSWin and OS X. The project is funded by donations, which he says are what let him keep working on it.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers prebuilt executables for Microsoft Windows, Apple OS X and Linux x86, plus source code, and tells users to read the notes on installing after downloading. Nothing on the homepage describes accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration. Some Linux distribution packages are modified and may behave differently from the upstream release, so the author asks users to retest with the unmodified download before reporting bugs. The brew entry lists 47 executables, including dispcal, dispread, colprof, spotread and targen.
brief.standout: It drives color measurement instruments directly through its own driver code, so a sensor can profile a real monitor from the command line. The homepage also says it contains what it calls the fastest portable 8 bit raster color conversion engine available anywhere.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage says it was last updated 2026/2/4 and lists current version 3.5.0 dated 4th February 2026, with downloads for that version.
brief.caveats: Licensed under AGPL, and the author points commercial users to a separate non-GPL licence for icclib and cgatslib. The author says there is little prospect of native Wayland display calibration support and recommends X11 for Linux users who need a color managed display. Instrument problems should go to the Argyll author or mailing list, not the instrument vendor. The brew caveats field was empty. I did not fetch the online documentation, so no command syntax was checked.
quotes: ArgyllCMS is an ICC compatible color management system, available as Open Source.
Argyll is a collection of source code that compiles into a set of command line tools, licensed under an AGPL license.
So my current advice for people wanting to use a color managed display on Linux is to stick to X11.
fetch_log: https://www.argyllcms.com/ - fetched OK. Homepage text only, no README. It links to online documentation, but the link URLs were not present in the returned text, so I did not follow them.
